key_insight: The ITE-Transformer combines pre-trained EHR representations with causal machine learning to estimate how treatment effects may vary across individual patients.
clinical_relevance: In oncology, the model could support real-world research comparing immunotherapy with chemotherapy, rather than discovering new drugs or establishing treatment recommendations.
method: Self-supervised pre-training on longitudinal diagnosis and medication histories.
Prediction of treatment assignment and treatment-specific outcome risks.
Doubly robust causal learning to estimate individualized treatment effects.
evidence_signal: Trained on structured EHRs from approximately 350,000 All of Us participants, the model improved treatment-assignment and outcome-model discrimination and calibration versus tabular models and a non-pre-trained transformer across diabetes and pan-cancer comparisons.
watch_item: Observational EHR estimates remain vulnerable to unmeasured confounding, and better predictive performance does not establish accurate individual causal effects.
paper_title: The ITE-Transformer: A pre-trained foundation model for predicting individualized treatment effects from electronic health records
